whyCorrect: Find the row whose UV index is 1, then read straight across to the Number of days column: 9. The table pairs each UV index value with a count of days, so nothing has to be added or subtracted here. The only work is making sure you read across the row rather than down the wrong column.

whyWrong.A: 4 is a UV index value, taken from the bottom of the first column, not a count of days.
whyWrong.C: 40 is 15 + 12 + 13, the number of days on which the UV index was something other than 1.
whyWrong.D: 49 is the total number of days in the study, stated in the sentence above the table.

tips: The day counts are the column that adds up to 49; that check tells you which column you are in.

whyCorrect: Match each number in 17h + 45 = 164 to a piece of the story. The 17 is multiplied by the hours, so it is the hourly rate; 45 stands alone with no h, so it is the onetime fee; 164 is what those two parts together come to, which is the total charge.

whyWrong.A: 45 is the onetime fee, because it is the term with no h attached to it.
whyWrong.B: h is the number of hours worked; 164 sits on the other side of the equation from h.
whyWrong.C: 17 is the charge per hour, since it is the number multiplied by the hours.

tips: A constant alone on the far side of the equals sign is almost always the total.

whyCorrect: Every temperature recorded was at least as large as the lowest reading and no larger than the highest, so 40 acts as a floor and 90 as a ceiling. Both bounds are needed at once, which is what \(40\leq t\leq 90\) says. A single inequality can only pin down one end of the range.

whyWrong.B: This turns the minimum into a maximum; it excludes every temperature above 40, including the 90 that was actually recorded.
whyWrong.C: 50 is the difference 90 - 40, the width of the range, not a temperature that bounds it.
whyWrong.D: This turns the maximum into a minimum; it excludes everything below 90, including the 40 that was actually recorded.

whyCorrect: Set 6(2x + 4) = 48 and divide both sides by 6 before touching the parentheses: 2x + 4 = 8. Then 2x = 4 and x = 2. Dividing by the outside factor first means you never have to distribute.

whyWrong.B: 6 is the factor outside the parentheses, not a solution; f(6) = 6(16) = 96.
whyWrong.C: 8 is the value of 2x + 4 after dividing by 6, which is one step short of solving for x.
whyWrong.D: 22 comes from setting 2x + 4 = 48 and ignoring the factor of 6 altogether.

whyCorrect: A ratio of 5 to 2 means the counts are 5 parts green for every 2 parts blue. Going from 2 blue to 16 blue multiplies the blue part by 8, so the green part must be multiplied by the same 8: 5 x 8 = 40. Scaling both parts by the same factor is exactly what keeps the ratio at 5 to 2.
commonMistakes: Writing \(\frac{5}{2}=\frac{16}{g}\) puts green and blue on the wrong sides and gives 6.4; green pairs with the 5.

whyCorrect: The points fall as x increases, from about y = 26 near x = 0.5 down to about y = 8 near x = 3.5, so the slope has to be negative. That drop of roughly 18 over 3 units of x gives a slope near -6, and extending the trend back to x = 0 puts the y-intercept near 28. Only y = 28 - 6x has both.

whyWrong.A: This has a steep positive slope of 28, so it rises while the data fall.
whyWrong.B: The slope is negative here, but the intercept of 6 is far too low: the leftmost data point is already near y = 26.
whyWrong.C: The intercept 28 is right, but the slope +6 makes the line rise where the data clearly fall.

tips: Decide the sign of the slope from the picture first; it usually eliminates half the choices before any arithmetic.

whyCorrect: Percentage by mass is the mass of the part divided by the mass of the whole sample: 189 / 900 = 0.21, which is 21%. The divisor is the full 900 g sample, not the water and not any rounded figure.

whyWrong.A: 9% of 900 g would be only 81 g of water, well under the 189 g measured.
whyWrong.B: 9.9% of 900 g is about 89 g, still only about half the water actually present.
whyWrong.C: 18.9% comes from dividing 189 by 1,000 instead of by the actual 900 g sample.

tips: 10% of 900 is 90; since 189 is more than twice that, the answer has to be over 20%.

whyCorrect: Read two lattice points off line n: it passes through (-1, -3) and (0, 3), so it rises 6 for every 1 unit right and its slope is 6. Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, so line k has slope \(-\frac{1}{6}\). The two steps are read the slope, then flip and negate it.

whyWrong.A: \(-\frac{1}{5}\) is the negative reciprocal of 5, but line n rises 6 units per unit of x, not 5.
whyWrong.C: 5 is neither line n's slope nor a negative reciprocal; a perpendicular slope must have the opposite sign from 6.
whyWrong.D: 6 is line n's own slope, so a line with this slope is parallel to n, not perpendicular.

whyCorrect: The intersection point lies on both graphs, so substitute x = 5 into each equation. The second gives 10 + ky = 22, so ky = 12. The first becomes 5m + ky = -83, and replacing ky with 12 gives 5m + 12 = -83, so 5m = -95 and m = -19. You never need k or y on their own, only the product ky.
tips: When two equations contain an identical term, solve for that whole term as if it were a single unknown.

whyCorrect: Slope is the change in y divided by the change in x between the two points, with the subtractions taken in the same order top and bottom: \(\frac{3-2}{3-0}=\frac{1}{3}\). Since the line is linear, that single pair of points fixes the slope everywhere.
commonMistakes: Writing the differences the other way up gives 3; the change in y always goes on top.

whyCorrect: Probability is the number of favourable pages over the number of pages altogether: 21 illustrated pages out of 250, so \(\frac{21}{250}\). It cannot be reduced, since 21 factors as 3 times 7 and 250 as 2 times 5 cubed, sharing no common factor.

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{250}{21}\) is upside down; it is larger than 1, and a probability never exceeds 1.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{11}{125}\) equals \(\frac{22}{250}\), which counts one illustrated page too many.
whyWrong.D: \(\frac{21}{251}\) adds a page to the total; the book has 250 pages, and the illustrated ones are part of that 250.

whyCorrect: Isolate the squared term first: subtracting 5c from both sides gives b squared = 9d - 5c. Undoing a square means taking a square root, and that produces both a positive and a negative root, so \(b=\pm\sqrt{9d-5c}\).

whyWrong.A: Dividing by 2 undoes multiplication by 2, not squaring, and the 5c is added rather than subtracted.
whyWrong.B: The subtraction is right but dividing by 2 is not how you undo a square; you need a square root.
whyWrong.C: The sign is wrong: moving 5c to the other side of the equals sign makes it -5c, not +5c.

whyCorrect: The volume of a cylinder is \(\pi r^{2}h\), so square the radius and then multiply by the height: \(\pi(18)^{2}(4)=\pi(324)(4)=1296\pi\). Only the radius gets squared.

whyWrong.A: \(4\pi\) uses the height alone and ignores the radius entirely.
whyWrong.B: \(22\pi\) adds 18 and 4 instead of multiplying the squared radius by the height.
whyWrong.C: \(288\pi\) squares the height instead of the radius: \(4^{2}\times 18=288\).

whyCorrect: A y-intercept is the point where the graph crosses the y-axis, which is where x = 0. Substituting x = 0 into 3x + 2y = 96 leaves 2y = 96, so y = 48 and the point is (0, 48).

whyWrong.A: 5 is the sum of the coefficients 3 and 2, which has nothing to do with where the line meets the y-axis.
whyWrong.B: 6 is the product of the coefficients 3 and 2, not a value of y.
whyWrong.C: 32 is 96 divided by 3, which is the x-intercept: it comes from setting y = 0 instead of x = 0.

whyCorrect: Subtract 12 from both sides to get \(\frac{6}{7}p=42\), then multiply by \(\frac{7}{6}\) to get p = 49. The question asks for 7p, so finish the job: 7 times 49 is 343.

whyWrong.A: 341 is a slip in the final multiplication; 7 times 49 is 350 - 7 = 343, not 341.
whyWrong.B: 342 is one short of 7 times 49; recompute 7 times 49 as 7 times 50 minus 7.
whyWrong.D: 346 is three more than 7 times 49, again a slip in the last multiplication rather than in the algebra.

tips: Once you have p = 49, note that 7p = 343 is exactly 7 cubed, which is an easy value to confirm.

whyCorrect: Growing by 3% a year multiplies the population by 1.03 each year, so after t years the starting value 1340 has been multiplied by 1.03 t times: \(N=1340(1.03)^{t}\). The starting amount is the coefficient and the yearly multiplier is the base of the exponent.

whyWrong.A: This makes 1340 the repeated multiplier, so the population would grow by a factor of 1340 every year.
whyWrong.B: Multiplying by 0.03 each year keeps only 3% of the population annually, a 97% drop, not a 3% rise.
whyWrong.D: This swaps the roles of the two numbers: 1.03 becomes the starting amount and 1340 the yearly multiplier.

whyCorrect: If x and y are both negative, then 7x and 4y are both negative, so 7x + 4y is negative and can never be greater than 12. In every other region one variable can be made arbitrarily large and positive, which is enough to push the sum past 12.

whyWrong.A: Try (10, 10): 70 + 40 = 110, which is greater than 12, so this region contains solutions.
whyWrong.B: A negative x can be swamped by a large positive y: (-1, 100) gives -7 + 400 = 393 > 12.
whyWrong.D: A large positive x can be swamped the other way: (100, -1) gives 700 - 4 = 696 > 12.

tips: To show a region does contain solutions you only need one point that works; to rule it out you must argue about every point in it.

whyCorrect: LK is parallel to RT and the side ST cuts across both of them, so angle SKL and angle STR sit in matching positions and are corresponding angles. Corresponding angles along a transversal are equal, and angle STR is angle T, which is 50°. The 10° at R is not needed.

whyWrong.A: 48 assumes angle SKL is smaller than angle T, but the parallel lines force the two to be equal.
whyWrong.B: 49 comes from adjusting angle T by a degree; the correspondence is exact, not approximate.
whyWrong.D: 53 comes from working with angle S, which is 180 - 10 - 50 = 120°, and then guessing at how the remaining 60° splits instead of using corresponding angles.

whyCorrect: The coefficient of \(x^{2}\) is negative, so the parabola opens downward and its highest point is the vertex. The vertex of \(y=ax^{2}+bx+c\) sits at \(x=-\frac{b}{2a}\), which here is \(-\frac{2400}{2(-100)}=12\).

whyWrong.A: 8 is the current ticket price in dollars; x measures the increase in price, not the price itself.
whyWrong.C: 24 comes from dividing 2400 by 100 and forgetting the factor of 2 in the denominator 2a.
whyWrong.D: 32 is a value of x where the revenue drops to zero, not where it peaks: substituting 32 gives y = 0.

whyCorrect: The equation is already in the form \((x-h)^{2}+(y-k)^{2}=r^{2}\), so a point lies on the circle exactly when \((x+3)^{2}+(y-4)^{2}\) comes out to 25. For this choice \(x+3=\sqrt{11}\) and \(y-4=\sqrt{14}\), giving 11 + 14 = 25.

whyWrong.A: (-3, 4) is the centre of the circle, which is 5 units from every point on it and lies on the circle itself only if the radius were 0.
whyWrong.B: Substituting gives \(6^{2}+(-8)^{2}=100\), not 25.
whyWrong.C: The signs on the 3 and the 4 are flipped, so \(x+3=\sqrt{11}+6\) and \(y-4=\sqrt{14}-8\), which do not square to a total of 25.

whyCorrect: Both fractions already share the denominator \(5x^{2}\), so add the numerators first: \(x^{20}(x-4)+4x^{20}=x^{20}(x-4+4)=x^{21}\). Dividing that by \(5x^{2}\) subtracts exponents, giving \(\frac{1}{5}x^{19}\), so c = 19.

whyWrong.A: 4 is the constant inside the parentheses; it cancels when the two numerators are combined and never becomes the exponent.
whyWrong.B: 5 is the coefficient in the denominator, which produces the \(\frac{1}{5}\) out front, not the power of x.
whyWrong.D: 21 is the exponent of the combined numerator; you still have to divide by \(x^{2}\), which drops it to 19.

whyCorrect: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles, so angle D equals angle A and the 2.4 scale factor changes no trig ratio at all. From \(\tan A=\frac{21}{20}\) the leg opposite A is 21 and the adjacent leg is 20, so the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{441+400}=\sqrt{841}=29\). Therefore \(\sin D=\sin A=\frac{21}{29}\).

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{29}{21}\) is the reciprocal, which is \(\csc D\); sine puts the opposite leg over the hypotenuse, so it must be less than 1.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{22}{29}\) uses 22 as the opposite leg, but the tangent ratio gives 21.
whyWrong.D: \(\frac{7}{10}\) is \(\frac{21}{30}\), which takes the hypotenuse to be 30; a right triangle with legs 20 and 21 has hypotenuse 29.

commonMistakes: Scaling the sides by 2.4 before computing the ratio wastes time and often introduces an error; angles and trig ratios are unchanged by similarity.

whyCorrect: Collect the x terms on one side and the numbers on the other. Subtracting 2x from both sides gives 2x - 7 = 15, then adding 7 gives 2x = 22, so x = 11. The step people drop is adding the 7 rather than subtracting it: it is on the left as -7, so it moves across as +7.

whyWrong.A: 8 is 15 - 7, which comes from subtracting the 7 instead of adding it when moving it across the equals sign.
whyWrong.B: 9 fails the check: 4(9) - 7 = 29 but 2(9) + 15 = 33, so the two sides are not equal.
whyWrong.D: 14 fails the check the other way: 4(14) - 7 = 49 but 2(14) + 15 = 43.

tips: Substituting your answer back into the original equation catches every slip here in about ten seconds.

whyCorrect: Distribute first: 3(x + 2) is 3x + 6, so the left side becomes 3x + 6 - 5 = 3x + 1. Setting 3x + 1 = 2x + 9 and subtracting 2x and 1 from both sides gives x = 8.

whyWrong.A: 5 fails the check: the left side is 3(7) - 5 = 16 while the right side is 19.
whyWrong.B: 6 fails the check: the left side is 3(8) - 5 = 19 while the right side is 21.
whyWrong.C: 7 comes from simplifying 6 - 5 as 2 instead of 1, which turns the left side into 3x + 2 and pushes the solution down by one.

whyCorrect: The y terms already have opposite signs, so add the two equations as they stand: (2x + y) + (x - y) = 11 + 1 gives 3x = 12, so x = 4. Adding eliminates y without any rearranging.

whyWrong.A: 3 is the value of y, not x; once x = 4, the first equation gives y = 11 - 8 = 3.
whyWrong.C: 5 does not satisfy both equations: 2(5) + y = 11 forces y = 1, and then x - y = 4, not 1.
whyWrong.D: 6 comes from dividing the sum 12 by 2 instead of by the 3 that x collects into.

whyCorrect: Add the two equations to eliminate y: 3x = 12, so x = 4. Substituting back into x - y = 1 gives y = 3, so x + y = 7. You can also get it in one step by noticing that adding the equations another way is unnecessary once x is known.
tips: The question asks for x + y, not x, so finish by finding the second variable rather than stopping at x = 4.

whyCorrect: Subtract 12 from both sides to get -4x > 16, then divide by -4. Dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the sign, so x < -4. Forgetting that reversal is the whole point of this question.

whyWrong.A: x > -4 has the right boundary value but keeps the original direction, which only holds if you divide by a positive number.
whyWrong.C: x > 4 loses the negative sign on the 4 and does not flip the inequality either.
whyWrong.D: x < 4 flips the inequality correctly but drops the negative sign on the boundary value.

commonMistakes: Test a value: x = -10 makes -4x + 12 = 52, which is greater than 28, so the solutions lie to the left of -4.

whyCorrect: The registration fee is paid once, so it is not multiplied by the hours: 30 + 25h = 205. Subtracting the fee first leaves 25h = 175, so h = 7. Take the one-time charge off the total before you divide.
commonMistakes: Dividing 205 by 25 straight away gives 8.2 because it charges the $30 fee as though it were hourly.

whyCorrect: Let g be the graph-paper notebooks; then the plain ones number 12 - g. The cost is 2(12 - g) + 3g = 29, which simplifies to 24 + g = 29, so g = 5. Each graph-paper notebook adds exactly $1 to the $24 baseline of twelve plain notebooks.

whyWrong.A: 3 graph-paper notebooks give 2(9) + 3(3) = $27, two dollars short.
whyWrong.B: 4 graph-paper notebooks give 2(8) + 3(4) = $28, one dollar short.
whyWrong.D: 6 graph-paper notebooks give 2(6) + 3(6) = $30, one dollar over.

tips: Start from all-cheap (12 notebooks at $2 = $24) and count how many dollars you need to add; that number is the count of the more expensive item.

whyCorrect: Find the slope first: \(\frac{16-7}{5-2}=\frac{9}{3}=3\). Then use either point in y = 3x + b; with (2, 7) you get 7 = 6 + b, so b = 1 and the y-intercept is (0, 1).

whyWrong.A: (0, -1) comes from a sign slip in 7 = 3(2) + b, solving as b = 6 - 7 instead of 7 - 6.
whyWrong.C: (0, 3) is the slope written as an intercept; 3 is how much y changes per unit of x, not where the line crosses the axis.
whyWrong.D: (0, 5) borrows the x-coordinate 5 from the second given point.

whyCorrect: Look for two numbers that multiply to -24 and add to -5: those are -8 and +3, so the equation factors as (x - 8)(x + 3) = 0. Setting each factor to zero gives x = 8 and x = -3.

whyWrong.B: x = 3 and x = -8 are the roots of \(x^{2}+5x-24=0\); both signs are flipped, so the middle term would come out +5x.
whyWrong.C: x = -4 and x = 6 multiply to -24 but add to +2, giving \(x^{2}-2x-24\).
whyWrong.D: x = 4 and x = -6 also multiply to -24 but add to -2, giving \(x^{2}+2x-24\).

tips: The two roots must multiply to the constant term and add to the negative of the x-coefficient; check both conditions, not just the product.

whyCorrect: The equation factors as (x - 8)(x + 3) = 0, so the solutions are 8 and -3 and their sum is 5. You can also read the sum straight off the equation: for \(x^{2}+bx+c=0\) the solutions always sum to -b, and here -b = 5.
tips: The sum-of-roots shortcut answers this without factoring at all, which is worth knowing when the numbers are ugly.

whyCorrect: Complete the square: half of -8 is -4, so \(x^{2}-8x+21=(x-4)^{2}+21-16=(x-4)^{2}+5\). A square is never negative, so the smallest the function can be is 5, reached at x = 4.

whyWrong.A: 3 would be the minimum if the constant left over were 3, but 21 - 16 = 5.
whyWrong.B: 4 is the x-value where the minimum occurs, not the minimum value itself.
whyWrong.D: 21 is f(0), the y-intercept; the graph keeps falling to the right of x = 0 until it reaches x = 4.

commonMistakes: Finding the vertex x = 4 and stopping there answers a different question; substitute it back to get f(4) = 5.

whyCorrect: Evaluate the exponent before anything else: with t = 12, \(\frac{t}{4}=3\), so the model gives \(500(2)^{3}=500\times 8=4000\). The population doubles every 4 hours, and 12 hours is exactly three doublings.

whyWrong.A: 3998 is what you get from a rounded decimal value of the power instead of the exact \(2^{3}=8\).
whyWrong.B: 3999 is likewise a rounding artefact; the arithmetic here is exact, with no decimals involved.
whyWrong.D: 4002 overshoots the exact product 500 times 8.

tips: When the exponent divides evenly, work it out as a whole number first so the answer comes out exact.

whyCorrect: Multiplying powers of the same base adds exponents and dividing subtracts them, so \(\frac{x^{3}\times x^{5}}{x^{2}}=x^{3+5-2}=x^{6}\). Handle the numerator first, then subtract the denominator's exponent.

whyWrong.A: \(x^{4}\) comes from dividing the exponents (8 divided by 2) instead of subtracting them.
whyWrong.C: \(x^{8}\) adds the numerator exponents correctly but never divides by \(x^{2}\).
whyWrong.D: \(x^{10}\) adds the denominator's exponent instead of subtracting it.

whyCorrect: A zero at x = r shows up as the factor (x - r), so a zero at -2 gives the factor (x + 2) and a zero at 5 gives (x - 5). The sign inside each factor is the opposite of the zero it produces.

whyWrong.A: (x - 2)(x + 5) has zeros at 2 and -5, both signs reversed from what is asked.
whyWrong.C: (x - 2)(x - 5) has zeros at 2 and 5, so the -2 is wrong.
whyWrong.D: (x + 2)(x + 5) has zeros at -2 and -5, so the 5 is wrong.

tips: Check a candidate by substituting the stated zeros; the correct function must give 0 for both x = -2 and x = 5.

whyCorrect: The number of real solutions is decided by the discriminant \(b^{2}-4ac\), which here is \(4^{2}-4(2)(7)=16-56=-40\). A negative discriminant means the square root is not a real number, so the parabola never crosses the x-axis and there are no real solutions.

whyWrong.B: Exactly one real solution requires a discriminant of 0, meaning the vertex just touches the x-axis.
whyWrong.C: Two real solutions requires a positive discriminant; here it is -40.
whyWrong.D: Infinitely many solutions only happens when the equation is an identity such as 0 = 0, never for a genuine quadratic.

tips: The parabola opens upward and its minimum value is 5, which is above the x-axis, so it cannot equal 0.

whyCorrect: Work a composition from the inside out. First \(g(2)=2^{2}-1=3\), and only then feed that result into f: f(3) = 2(3) + 3 = 9. The 2 goes into g, not into f.

whyWrong.A: 7 is f(2), which applies the outer function directly to 2 and skips g altogether.
whyWrong.B: 8 is an arithmetic slip in the last step; 2(3) + 3 is 9, not 8.
whyWrong.D: 11 comes from evaluating g(2) as \(2^{2}=4\) and forgetting the -1, then computing f(4) = 11.

tips: Write down the inner value on its own line before touching the outer function; that alone prevents most composition errors.

whyCorrect: The mean is the total divided by how many values there are. Adding gives 72 + 85 + 90 + 68 + 75 = 390, and 390 divided by 5 is 78.

whyWrong.A: 76 corresponds to a total of 380, ten short of the true sum of 390.
whyWrong.B: 77 corresponds to a total of 385, five short.
whyWrong.D: 80 corresponds to a total of 400, which comes from rounding the scores up before adding.

tips: Add the scores in pairs that make round numbers (72 + 68 = 140, 85 + 75 = 160) to keep the sum reliable.

whyCorrect: Sort the values first: 9, 14, 18, 22, 25, 31. With an even count there is no single middle value, so average the two in the middle: (18 + 22) / 2 = 20.

whyWrong.A: 18 is only the lower of the two middle values; with six values you must average both.
whyWrong.B: 19 is close to the mean of the set, which is about 19.8, but the mean and the median are different measures.
whyWrong.D: 22 is only the upper of the two middle values.

commonMistakes: Taking the middle of the list as it is printed, without sorting, gives 9 and 31 as the central pair.

whyCorrect: A red-to-total ratio of 5 to 8 means red makes up \(\frac{5}{8}\) of the marbles. Divide the total into eighths first: 136 divided by 8 is 17, and five of those parts give 5 times 17 = 85.

whyWrong.A: 75 is five-eighths of 120, so it comes from dividing 136 by 8 and getting 15.
whyWrong.B: 80 is five-eighths of 128, from getting 16 instead of 17 for the eighth.
whyWrong.D: 90 is five-eighths of 144, from getting 18 instead of 17.

tips: Because the ratio is red to total (not red to blue), the 8 is already the whole bag; there is nothing to add.

whyCorrect: The area of a triangle is half the base times the height: \(\frac{1}{2}(14)(9)=63\) square centimetres. Multiply the two given lengths and then halve, once.

whyWrong.A: 31.5 halves the product twice; 126 divided by 2 is 63, and dividing again is one step too many.
whyWrong.C: 126 is 14 times 9 with the factor of one half left out, which is the area of a rectangle with those dimensions.
whyWrong.D: 252 doubles the product instead of halving it.

whyCorrect: The area of a circle is \(\pi r^{2}\), so square the radius before multiplying: \(\pi(6)^{2}=36\pi\). Asking for the answer in terms of \(\pi\) means leaving \(\pi\) as a symbol rather than multiplying it out as 113.1.

whyWrong.B: \(6\pi\) uses the radius itself instead of its square; it is half the circumference, not the area.
whyWrong.C: \(66\pi\) matches neither formula: the area is \(36\pi\) and the circumference is \(12\pi\).
whyWrong.D: This choice restates the same value as an approximation, but the question asks for the exact area in terms of \(\pi\), which is what choice A gives.

commonMistakes: Squaring is applied to the radius only, not to \(\pi\), so the answer is \(36\pi\) and not \(36\pi^{2}\).

whyCorrect: The hypotenuse comes from \(a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}\): \(9^{2}+12^{2}=81+144=225\), and the square root of 225 is 15. The legs 9 and 12 are the 3-4-5 triple multiplied by 3.

whyWrong.A: 13 is the hypotenuse of the 5-12-13 triple, recalled by reflex; \(13^{2}=169\), not 225.
whyWrong.C: 18 is twice the shorter leg; \(18^{2}=324\), far more than 225.
whyWrong.D: 21 is 9 + 12, which adds the legs instead of using the Pythagorean theorem.

tips: The hypotenuse must be longer than either leg but shorter than their sum, which already rules out 21.

whyCorrect: One mile is 1.6 kilometres, so a distance in miles becomes a larger number in kilometres: multiply. 49 times 1.6 is 78.4 kilometres per hour.

whyWrong.A: 30.6 is 49 divided by 1.6, which converts in the wrong direction and turns kilometres into miles.
whyWrong.B: 47.4 subtracts 1.6 from 49; a unit conversion scales a quantity, it does not shift it.
whyWrong.C: 50.6 adds 1.6 to 49, the same mistake in the other direction.

tips: Kilometres are shorter than miles, so the numerical answer must be bigger than 49; that eliminates three choices at once.

whyCorrect: Multiply every term of the first factor by every term of the second: \(3x^{3}\) gives \(15x^{5}+24x^{4}\), \(-x^{2}\) gives \(-5x^{4}-8x^{3}\), and 4 gives \(20x^{2}+32x\). Combining the two \(x^{4}\) terms, 24 - 5 = 19, produces \(15x^{5}+19x^{4}-8x^{3}+20x^{2}+32x\).

whyWrong.A: The last two terms lose a power of x each: 4 times \(5x^{2}\) is \(20x^{2}\), not -20x, and 4 times 8x is 32x, not 32.
whyWrong.B: The \(x^{2}\) term has the wrong sign (4 times \(5x^{2}\) is positive) and the final term is missing its x.
whyWrong.D: \(29x^{4}\) adds 24 and 5 instead of subtracting; the \(-x^{2}\) makes that term \(-5x^{4}\).

tips: Since every term of the second factor has an x in it, no constant term can survive; a constant in the answer is a signal to recheck.

whyCorrect: The question asks for x + 1, which is already the whole quantity multiplied by 5. Dividing both sides of 5(x + 1) = 25 by 5 gives x + 1 = 5 directly, with no need to expand or to solve for x.

whyWrong.A: 4 is the value of x; the question asks for x + 1, which is one more.
whyWrong.C: 19 comes from subtracting 5 from 25 and then subtracting a further 1, treating the 5 as something to remove rather than to divide by.
whyWrong.D: 20 comes from subtracting 5 from 25 instead of dividing by 5.

tips: When a question asks for an expression rather than for x, check whether that whole expression is already sitting inside the equation.

whyCorrect: Find the two times separately, then subtract. The curve reaches 20 million cells per mL at roughly x = 35 minutes and reaches 30 million at roughly x = 50 minutes, so the increase takes about 15 minutes. The question asks for an elapsed time, which is a difference of two x-values, not an x-value on its own.

whyWrong.B: 20 is the starting concentration in millions of cells per mL, read off the y-axis and mistaken for a time.
whyWrong.C: 30 is the ending concentration, again a y-value rather than an elapsed time.
whyWrong.D: 35 is the time at which the concentration first reaches 20 million; you still have to subtract it from the time at 30 million.

tips: Mark both crossing points on the x-axis before doing anything else, so the answer is visibly a gap rather than a single reading.

whyCorrect: Expand the left side: \((x+3)^{2}=x^{2}+6x+9\), so \(x^{2}+6x+9=30\). The expression asked for is everything except that 9, so subtract it: \(x^{2}+6x=21\). You never have to find x itself.

whyWrong.B: 30 is the value of \(x^{2}+6x+9\); the constant 9 has not been removed.
whyWrong.C: 39 adds 9 to 30 instead of subtracting it, which would match \((x+3)^{2}+9\).
whyWrong.D: 60 doubles 30, which corresponds to no step in the expansion.

tips: Expand and compare term by term with what is being asked; problems like this rarely require solving for x.

whyCorrect: Both equations are lines, and their slopes are 5 and 2. Different slopes mean the lines are not parallel, so they cross exactly once. Setting 5x = 2x + 2 confirms it: 3x = 2 gives the single solution \(x=\frac{2}{3}\).

whyWrong.B: Two straight lines cannot cross twice; two intersection points require at least one curved graph.
whyWrong.C: Infinitely many solutions would need the two equations to describe the same line, which would mean identical slopes and identical intercepts.
whyWrong.D: Zero solutions would need the lines to be parallel, that is, to have equal slopes; 5 and 2 are different.

whyCorrect: An absolute value is never negative, so 3k must be at least 0 and k cannot be negative. Dropping the bars the positive way gives 71 - 2k = 3k, so 5k = 71 and \(k=\frac{71}{5}\); the other case, 2k - 71 = 3k, gives k = -71, which is negative and therefore rejected. Checking: \(f(\frac{71}{5})=|71-28.4|=42.6\), which is indeed 3 times 14.2.

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{71}{2}\) is what makes the inside of the absolute value zero, so f(k) = 0 while 3k = 53.5.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{213}{5}\) is the value of f(k), that is 3k itself, not k.
whyWrong.D: 71 gives f(71) = |71 - 142| = 71, but 3k would be 213.

commonMistakes: Solving both absolute-value cases without checking the sign of the right-hand side leaves an extraneous solution in the answer set.

whyCorrect: Distribute first: g(x) = 2(16x - 17) = 32x - 34, so y = g(x) - 3 = 32x - 37. The y-intercept is the value at x = 0, which is -37.

whyWrong.B: -34 is g(0), which leaves out the -3 that the new function subtracts.
whyWrong.C: -20 is -17 - 3, which forgets to distribute the 2 across the parentheses.
whyWrong.D: -17 is the constant inside the parentheses, before either the doubling or the subtraction of 3.

tips: Subtracting 3 from a function shifts its whole graph down 3, so the intercept moves from -34 to -37.

whyCorrect: Slope is the change in y over the change in x, and the unknown n cancels in the subtraction: from (0, n) to (4, n + 19) the rise is (n + 19) - n = 19 while the run is 4, so the slope is \(\frac{19}{4}\). The next pair gives the same thing, (n + 38) - (n + 19) = 19 over 4, which confirms the relationship really is linear.
tips: An unknown constant that appears in every y-value always cancels in a difference, so do not let it stop you.

whyCorrect: A quadratic has exactly one solution when its discriminant is zero. Here \(b^{2}-4ac=24^{2}-4(18)c=576-72c\), and setting that equal to 0 gives 72c = 576, so c = 8.
tips: Exactly one solution means the parabola touches the x-axis at its vertex; you can check by confirming \(18x^{2}+24x+8=2(3x+2)^{2}\).

whyCorrect: Treat (x - 3) and (y + 9) as single blocks. The two equations have -8(y + 9) and +8(y + 9), so adding them eliminates that block entirely: 2(x - 3) = 129 + 432 = 561. The question asks for 8(x - 3), which is four times 2(x - 3), so multiply 561 by 4 to get 2244.
tips: There is no need to find x itself; scaling the quantity you already have avoids a messy division by 2.

whyCorrect: The base is a square of area 144, so each base edge is 12. Volume is base area times height, so the height is 2448 divided by 144 = 17. A lateral face is a rectangle with the base edge on one side and the height on the other: 12 times 17 = 204.

whyWrong.A: 17 is the height of the prism, which is only one side of the lateral face.
whyWrong.C: 540 corresponds to a 12 by 45 rectangle; the height here is 17, not 45.
whyWrong.D: 816 is 4 times 204, the combined area of all four lateral faces, but the question asks for just one.

tips: Take the square root of the base area first; that edge length is what the lateral face shares with the base.

whyCorrect: Set the two expressions for y equal and factor rather than expanding: \(5(x-2)^{2}=10(x-2)\) becomes \(5(x-2)[(x-2)-2]=0\), so x = 2 or x = 4. With x = 4 the second equation gives y = 10(2) = 20, so x + y = 24. The other solution, (2, 0), gives x + y = 2, which is not offered.

whyWrong.A: -20 has the sign of the y-value reversed; y = 10(4 - 2) is positive 20.
whyWrong.B: 4 is the x-coordinate on its own, not the sum x + y.
whyWrong.C: 20 is the y-coordinate on its own, again not the sum.

commonMistakes: Dividing both sides by (x - 2) discards the solution x = 2; factor instead of cancelling.

whyCorrect: A parabola is symmetric about the vertical line through its vertex, so the vertex x-value sits exactly halfway between the two x-intercepts. That gives \(\frac{39+p}{2}=14\), so 39 + p = 28 and p = -11. Equivalently, 39 is 25 units to the right of 14, so the other intercept is 25 units to the left.

whyWrong.A: -13 puts the midpoint of the intercepts at 13, not at the given 14.
whyWrong.B: -12 puts the midpoint at 13.5.
whyWrong.D: -8 puts the midpoint at 15.5.

tips: The value of m never matters here; only the x-coordinate of the vertex does.

whyCorrect: Cross-multiply and cancel one factor of x: \(x(x+1)=5kx^{2}\) becomes x + 1 = 5kx, so \(x=\frac{1}{5k-1}\). Setting that equal to \(\frac{1}{174}\) gives 5k - 1 = 174, so 5k = 175 and k = 35.

whyWrong.A: 33 gives 5k - 1 = 164, so the solution would be \(\frac{1}{164}\).
whyWrong.B: 34 gives 5k - 1 = 169, so the solution would be \(\frac{1}{169}\); this comes from forgetting the -1 and rounding.
whyWrong.D: 38 gives 5k - 1 = 189, so the solution would be \(\frac{1}{189}\).

tips: Substituting \(x=\frac{1}{174}\) into the original equation works too, but solving for x in terms of k first keeps the arithmetic small.

whyCorrect: Write the area formula with the given expressions: \(\frac{1}{2}(2x+6)(x-2)=x^{2}\). The left side factors as (x + 3)(x - 2), which expands to \(x^{2}+x-6\), so \(x^{2}+x-6=x^{2}\); the \(x^{2}\) terms cancel and x = 6.

whyWrong.A: x = 4 gives a base of 14 and a height of 2, an area of 14, but \(x^{2}=16\).
whyWrong.B: x = 5 gives a base of 16 and a height of 3, an area of 24, but \(x^{2}=25\).
whyWrong.D: x = 9 gives a base of 24 and a height of 7, an area of 84, but \(x^{2}=81\).

tips: Halving the base first turns 2x + 6 into x + 3 and keeps the multiplication clean.

whyWrong.A: -121 is -39(3) - 4, which drops the square in \((x+1)^{2}\) when evaluating g(2), and then reports that value instead of the difference.
whyWrong.B: 0 assumes 0 and 2 are mirror images about the vertex, but the axis of symmetry is x = -1, so 0 pairs with -2, not with 2.
whyWrong.C: 117 is g(0) - g(1) = -43 + 160, using the given point (1, -160) as though it were g(2).

tips: Symmetry about x = -1 gives g(0) = g(-2) = -43 for free, so only g(2) needs to be computed.

whyCorrect: Congruent triangles have equal corresponding angles, and F corresponds to C. In triangle ABC the angles sum to 180°, so angle C = 180 - 90 - 62 = 28°, and therefore angle F is 28° as well.

whyWrong.B: 62° is angle A, which corresponds to angle D, not to angle F.
whyWrong.C: 90° is angle B, which corresponds to angle E.
whyWrong.D: 118° is 180 - 62, the supplement of angle A, but no angle of a right triangle can exceed 90°.

tips: In a right triangle the two acute angles are complementary, so angle C is simply 90 - 62.

whyCorrect: Only the hours after the first are billed at 204, and there are h - 1 of those: C(h) = 408 + 204(h - 1) = 204h + 204. The check that settles it is h = 1, where the charge must be exactly 408, and 204(1) + 204 = 408.

whyWrong.B: At h = 1 this gives 204 + 408 = 612; it bills the first hour twice, once inside the 408 and once at the 204 rate.
whyWrong.C: At h = 1 this gives 408 + 204 = 612 as well, because it charges the 408 first-hour rate for every hour.
whyWrong.D: At h = 1 this gives 408 + 612 = 1020, more than twice the stated first-hour charge.

tips: Test any candidate function at h = 1, where the answer is given to you in the first sentence.

whyCorrect: The exponent is x - 60, so at x = 60 the power \((0.997)^{0}\) equals 1 and y = 22 + 47 = 69. That makes 47 exactly 22 less than the sound pressure level at 60 hertz. The 47 is also the level the model approaches as x grows, but the choices are about a specific frequency.

whyWrong.B: The model is only defined for \(x\geq 60\), so it says nothing about 0 hertz.
whyWrong.C: The estimated level at 60 hertz is 69, not 47; the 22 has been left out.
whyWrong.D: This combines both errors: it uses a frequency outside the model's domain and drops the 22.

tips: Whenever an exponent is written as x - c, substitute x = c first; the power collapses to 1 and the structure of the model becomes obvious.

whyCorrect: The second equation is exactly 3 times the first, so the two graphs are the same line and every point on 3x + 5y = 8 works. Solving that for x in terms of y gives \(x=\frac{8-5y}{3}=\frac{-5y}{3}+\frac{8}{3}\), so letting y = r produces the point \((\frac{-5r}{3}+\frac{8}{3},\,r)\).

whyWrong.A: This puts the x-expression in the y-slot; substituting gives \(3r+5(\frac{-5r}{3}+\frac{8}{3})\), which is not 8 except at one value of r.
whyWrong.B: Solving 3x + 5y = 8 for y gives \(y=\frac{-3x}{5}+\frac{8}{5}\); this choice has the slope positive instead of negative.
whyWrong.D: Substituting gives \(3(\frac{r}{3}+8)+5(\frac{-r}{3}+24)=r+144-\frac{5r}{3}\), which is not 8.

tips: Test a candidate by putting r = 0 into it and checking the resulting point in 3x + 5y = 8.

whyCorrect: Because a and b are parallel, each transversal meets them at the same angle, so v measures how line d is tilted against the parallels and z does the same for line e. Line c, together with line b and one of those transversals, cuts off a triangle whose third angle is the supplement of y, namely 180 - 136 = 44°. That gives x = 180 - 44 - v = 136 - v and, in the same way, w = 136 - z. Since v < z, subtracting the smaller number leaves the larger result, so x > w.

whyWrong.A: x < w would follow only if v were greater than z, and the problem states the opposite.
whyWrong.C: x = w requires v = z, which would make lines d and e parallel to each other; the figure and the given inequality rule that out.
whyWrong.D: Nothing forces the two angles to be complementary: x + w = 272 - v - z, which varies with v and z.

tips: Write each unknown angle in terms of the given ones before comparing; guessing from the figure fails because it is explicitly not to scale.

whyCorrect: P is multiplying the whole bracket, so undo it by dividing, not by subtracting: \(\frac{A}{P}=1+r\). Then subtract 1 from both sides to isolate r, giving \(r=\frac{A}{P}-1\).

whyWrong.B: Subtracting P undoes addition, but P is multiplied by the bracket, so it has to be divided out.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{P}{A}\) inverts the ratio; dividing both sides by P leaves A on top.
whyWrong.D: Adding 1 moves the 1 the wrong way; it is on the right side as +1, so it comes off as -1.

tips: Check with numbers: P = 100 and r = 0.2 give A = 120, and \(\frac{120}{100}-1=0.2\).

whyCorrect: An absolute value equation splits into two cases: 2x - 5 = 9 gives x = 7, and 2x - 5 = -9 gives x = -2. The question asks for the sum, so add both solutions: 7 + (-2) = 5.

whyWrong.A: 2 is the size of the negative solution with its sign dropped; the solution is -2, and dropping the sign changes the sum.
whyWrong.C: 7 is only the positive solution; the negative case still has to be solved and included.
whyWrong.D: 9 is the value the absolute value equals, not a solution of the equation.

tips: The two solutions are always symmetric about the value that makes the inside zero, here x = 2.5, so their sum is twice that.

whyCorrect: A linear system has no solution when the lines are parallel: the x- and y-coefficients must be in the same ratio while the constants are not. Matching 3 to 6 means the second equation is twice the first, so k must satisfy 2k = 8, giving k = 4. The constants confirm it, since 2 times 12 is 24, not 20, so the lines really are distinct.

whyWrong.A: 2 is the ratio between the x-coefficients (6 divided by 3), not the value of k itself.
whyWrong.C: 6 is copied from the x-coefficient of the second equation and makes the slopes different, so the lines would cross once.
whyWrong.D: 8 copies the y-coefficient of the second equation, as though the coefficients had to be identical rather than proportional.

tips: Check the constants too: if they scale by the same factor, the system has infinitely many solutions rather than none.

whyCorrect: Find the gallons per mile first: 3 gallons over 75 miles is 0.04 gallons per mile. Multiplying by 275 miles gives 11 gallons. Setting up the proportion \(\frac{3}{75}=\frac{g}{275}\) and cross-multiplying gives the same thing.
tips: 275 is 75 times \(\frac{11}{3}\), so scaling 3 gallons by that same factor lands on 11 without decimals.

whyCorrect: Follow the order the problem gives. Raising the price by 15% multiplies it by 1.15, so the price becomes 1.15P; the $10 discount is then taken off that, giving 1.15P - 10 = 131. The discount is a flat amount, so it is subtracted after the scaling, not before.

whyWrong.B: This takes the $10 off first and then raises the reduced price by 15%, which is the opposite order and a different final price.
whyWrong.C: Adding 0.15 adds fifteen cents; a 15% increase multiplies the price by 1.15.
whyWrong.D: Adding the 10 treats the discount as a surcharge.

tips: Percent changes multiply, flat fees and discounts add or subtract; the order in the sentence decides which happens first.

whyCorrect: The driver's weight counts against the load, so subtract it first: 1200 - 180 = 1020 pounds are available for boxes. Dividing by 35 gives about 29.1, and since a box cannot be partly loaded you round down to 29. Rounding up to 30 would need 1050 pounds of boxes, which is over the limit.
commonMistakes: Rounding 29.1 up to 30 is the usual error here; a maximum-load constraint always rounds down.

whyCorrect: Distribute both brackets, keeping the -2 attached to everything in the second: 5(2x - 3) = 10x - 15 and -2(x - 4) = -2x + 8. Combining gives 10x - 2x = 8x and -15 + 8 = -7, so the result is 8x - 7. The sign that trips people up is the -2 times -4, which is positive 8.

whyWrong.B: 8x - 23 comes from -2 times -4 giving -8 instead of +8, so the constants read -15 - 8.
whyWrong.C: 12x - 7 adds 10x and 2x instead of subtracting; the whole second bracket is being taken away.
whyWrong.D: 12x - 23 makes both of those errors at once.

tips: Substitute x = 0 into the original expression: it gives -15 + 8 = -7, which pins the constant term immediately.

whyCorrect: Add 4 to both sides first, so \(\frac{2}{3}x=14\). Then multiply by the reciprocal \(\frac{3}{2}\): \(x=14\times\frac{3}{2}=21\). Multiplying by \(\frac{3}{2}\) is the step that undoes multiplication by \(\frac{2}{3}\).
commonMistakes: Multiplying 14 by \(\frac{2}{3}\) instead of by its reciprocal gives about 9.3, which fails when substituted back.

whyCorrect: Multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second: 2x times x is \(2x^{2}\), 2x times 4 is 8x, -3 times x is -3x, and -3 times 4 is -12. The two middle terms combine as 8x - 3x = 5x, giving \(2x^{2}+5x-12\).

whyWrong.B: -5x reverses the middle terms, as if the products were -8x and +3x.
whyWrong.C: +11x adds 8x and 3x, which treats the -3 as +3.
whyWrong.D: -11x treats both the -3 and the +4 as having the opposite sign.

tips: The constant term is just -3 times 4 = -12, and the middle coefficient must be 8 - 3; checking those two numbers separates all four choices.

whyCorrect: A fractional exponent has the denominator as the root and the numerator as the power: \(27^{\frac{2}{3}}=(\sqrt[3]{27})^{2}\). The cube root of 27 is 3, and \(3^{2}=9\). Taking the root first keeps the numbers small.

whyWrong.A: 7 fails the check that the answer cubed must equal \(27^{2}=729\); \(7^{3}=343\).
whyWrong.B: 8 comes from cubing the 2 in the exponent rather than applying the exponent to 27.
whyWrong.D: 11 also fails the cube check, since \(11^{3}=1331\).

tips: If you square first you get 729, and the cube root of 729 is still 9, but the arithmetic is much heavier.

whyCorrect: Set the two expressions for y equal: \(x-1=x^{2}-4x+3\) rearranges to \(x^{2}-5x+4=0\), which factors as (x - 1)(x - 4) = 0. The x-coordinates of the intersections are 1 and 4, so the greater one is 4.

whyWrong.A: 1 is the smaller of the two intersection points, not the greater.
whyWrong.B: 2 is the x-coordinate of the parabola's vertex, which is not where the line crosses it.
whyWrong.C: 3 is an x-intercept of the parabola (where y = 0), but the line is not at y = 0 there.

tips: Substitute your x back into y = x - 1 to confirm the point: x = 4 gives y = 3, and the parabola at x = 4 also gives 16 - 16 + 3 = 3.

whyCorrect: Simplify the exponent first: with t = 6, \(\frac{t}{3}=2\), so \(A(6)=800(0.5)^{2}=800\times 0.25=200\). The substance halves every 3 years, and 6 years is exactly two halvings: 800 to 400 to 200.

whyWrong.A: 198 comes from carrying a rounded decimal through the calculation; the exponent is a whole number, so the result is exact.
whyWrong.B: 199 is likewise a rounding artefact rather than the exact quarter of 800.
whyWrong.D: 202 overshoots one quarter of 800.

tips: When the time is a whole number of half-lives, just halve repeatedly and skip the exponent arithmetic.

whyCorrect: The numerator is a difference of squares: \(x^{2}-9=(x-3)(x+3)\). The (x - 3) factor cancels with the denominator, which is legal because the question restricts x from being 3, leaving x + 3.

whyWrong.A: x - 3 is the factor that cancels away, not the one that survives.
whyWrong.C: \(x^{2}-3\) comes from cancelling a single x out of \(x^{2}\) and out of the denominator, but only whole factors can be cancelled, never individual terms.
whyWrong.D: x + 9 keeps the 9 from \(x^{2}-9\); factoring a difference of squares uses the square root of 9, which is 3.

tips: Confirm with a number: at x = 5 the original is \(\frac{16}{2}=8\), and x + 3 gives 8 as well.

whyCorrect: The path is a downward parabola, so the greatest height is at the vertex, \(t=-\frac{b}{2a}=-\frac{64}{2(-16)}=2\) seconds. Substituting t = 2 gives h = -16(4) + 64(2) + 5 = -64 + 128 + 5 = 69 feet. Finding the time of the peak is only half the job; you still have to evaluate the height there.

whyWrong.A: 5 feet is h(0), the height at the moment of release.
whyWrong.C: 64 is the coefficient of t, the initial upward speed in feet per second, not a height.
whyWrong.D: 133 is 64(2) + 5, which drops the \(-16t^{2}\) term when substituting t = 2.

tips: Answer choices that repeat a number straight out of the equation, like 5 and 64, are usually there for students who stop early.

whyCorrect: Substitute carefully, keeping the brackets around the negative number: \(f(-2)=3(-2)^{2}-2(-2)+1\). That is 3(4) = 12, then -2 times -2 = +4, then +1, so f(-2) = 17. Both the square and the middle term turn positive.

whyWrong.A: 9 comes from 12 - 4 + 1, treating -2 times -2 as -4 instead of +4.
whyWrong.B: 13 is 12 + 1, dropping the middle term entirely.
whyWrong.D: 21 is 12 + 8 + 1, which squares in the wrong place by treating the middle term as \(-2x^{2}\).

tips: Write the substitution with brackets, \(3(-2)^{2}\), before simplifying; most sign errors here come from omitting them.

whyCorrect: Pull out the largest perfect square inside the radical: 48 = 16 times 3, so \(\sqrt{48}=\sqrt{16}\times\sqrt{3}=4\sqrt{3}\). Simplest radical form means nothing left under the root has a perfect-square factor, and 3 does not.

whyWrong.B: \(3\sqrt{4}\) is 3 times 2 = 6, which is \(\sqrt{36}\), not \(\sqrt{48}\).
whyWrong.C: \(2\sqrt{12}\) has the same value as \(\sqrt{48}\), but it is not simplified: 12 still contains the perfect square 4, and reducing it gives \(4\sqrt{3}\).

tips: Square each candidate: only \(4\sqrt{3}\) and \(2\sqrt{12}\) square to 48, and of those only \(4\sqrt{3}\) is fully simplified.

whyCorrect: Percent increase compares the change to the original amount, not to the new one. The change is 300 - 240 = 60, and \(\frac{60}{240}=0.25\), so the revenue rose 25%.

whyWrong.A: 15% is \(\frac{60}{400}\); neither 400 nor anything like it appears in the problem.
whyWrong.B: 20% is \(\frac{60}{300}\), which divides the change by the new revenue instead of the original.
whyWrong.D: 30% is \(\frac{60}{200}\), again the wrong base.

tips: A quick sanity check: 25% of 240 is 60, and 240 + 60 = 300.

whyCorrect: Count the total first: 6 + 4 + 10 = 20 marbles. The probability of blue is the 4 blue marbles over all 20, which is \(\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{5}\).

whyWrong.B: \(\frac{1}{4}\) is \(\frac{4}{16}\), dividing by the 16 marbles that are not blue instead of by all 20.
whyWrong.C: \(\frac{2}{5}\) is \(\frac{8}{20}\), which doubles the number of blue marbles.
whyWrong.D: \(\frac{1}{2}\) is \(\frac{10}{20}\), the probability of drawing green.

tips: The denominator of a simple probability is always the whole sample space, so add every category before you divide.

whyCorrect: In y = mx + b the slope tells you how much the predicted y changes for a one-unit increase in x. Here x is hours studied and y is exam score, so 4.5 means one extra hour of study is associated with about 4.5 more predicted points.

whyWrong.B: The predicted score at zero hours is the intercept, 62, not the slope.
whyWrong.C: This reverses the roles of the variables; the model predicts score from hours, not hours from score.
whyWrong.D: A slope is a rate of change, not a ceiling; this line has no maximum value.

tips: Read the slope as "units of y per one unit of x" and the sentence writes itself.

whyCorrect: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height: 5 times 4 is 20, and 20 times 3 is 60 cubic centimetres. All three dimensions are multiplied, none added.

whyWrong.A: 58 is short of the product; 5 times 4 times 3 is exactly 60.
whyWrong.B: 59 is one short of the exact product.
whyWrong.D: 62 is two over.

commonMistakes: Adding the dimensions gives 12 and computing surface area gives 2(20 + 15 + 12) = 94; neither is the volume.

whyCorrect: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Adding the two given angles gives 42 + 65 = 107, so the third angle is 180 - 107 = 73°.

whyWrong.A: 63° results from adding 42 and 65 as 117 rather than 107.
whyWrong.C: 83° results from adding them as 97.
whyWrong.D: 107° is the sum of the two given angles, which is the amount to subtract from 180, not the answer.

tips: Check by adding all three: 42 + 65 + 73 = 180.
